To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chemoattractants cause rapid release of the human polymorphonucloear IL-1 type 2 decoy receptor, which is a mechanism that may regulate leukocyte recruitment in vivo.

chemotactic peptides cause rapid release of the decoy IL-1 receptor II from human neutrophils, and that this release is independent of protein synthesis and mediated by the chemoattractants' activation of the signal-transducing pathways of neutrophils.
the chemoattractants formyl-Met-leu-Phe (fMLP) and interleukin 8 (IL-8) cause a rapid and reversible loss in the binding of interleukin 11 to human polymorphonucleated leukocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the IL- 1 type II receptor in the regulation of leukocyte functions.
the regulation of the expression of the IL- 1 type II receptor (IL- 1RII) by human polymorphonuclar leukocytes (PMNs).
the role of the IL- 1 type II receptor (IL- 1R) in the regulation of IL-1 activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the release of the decoy receptor by chemokine is a mechanism that allows the cells to respond to IL-1 and other chemokines.
chemokines induce rapid release of IL-1 type 2 decoy receptors in human polymorpho-nuclear cells, which is consistent with a role for these receptors in leukocyte recruitment.
the IL-1 receptor II is a decoy receptor that does not transduce a signal, and that it is released from PMN upon activation with FMLP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the release of the IL1 decoy receptor is not a mechanism for the control of IL1 activity in the inflammatory response.
the IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1ra) is a natural inhibitor of inflammation, and that it may be a useful therapeutic agent in the treatment of inflammatory disease.
the IL-1R II is shed from PMN and monocyte surfaces in response to chemokines and that the shed receptor can be recovered from the culture supernatants of these cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the IL-1RII is a dynamic molecule that is released from the PMN cell surface in response to chemoattractants, and that this is a regulated process involving elements of the signal transduction pathways of chemoattracts.
chemoattractants can induce rapid release of IL-1RII in PMN, a cell type that predominantly expresses this receptor.
chemoattractants cause a rapid loss of the IL- 1 type II receptor (IL- 1 decoy R) in human polymorpho-nuclear leukocytes (neutro-phil).
